s01.text: A seven-billion-parameter model runs on a laptop in fourteen gigabytes.

s02.text: Training the same model needs a hundred and twelve.

s03.text: That gap is arithmetic. It is worth doing carefully, because every term in it is a decision somebody made.

s04.text: Start with the weights. Seven billion parameters at sixteen bits each is fourteen gigabytes.

s05.text: Training also needs the gradients. Another fourteen gigabytes.

s06.text: Then the optimizer. Adam keeps two running averages per parameter, momentum and variance, in full precision.

s07.text: That is eight bytes per parameter. Two more copies of the model, held as state.

s08.text: Fourteen, plus fourteen, plus fifty-six. Eighty-four gigabytes before a single activation.

s09.text: Activations scale with batch size and sequence length, not with model size.

s10.text: So the honest total depends on your configuration. At batch one and sequence four thousand, it lands near a hundred and twelve gigabytes.

s11.text: You can make it fit. Shard it across eight GPUs, and each one holds an eighth.

s12.text: But sharding does not delete the memory. It splits it, and adds the cost of the GPUs talking to each other.

s13.text: A model you cannot fit is a model you cannot run. That is why training costs what it costs.
